questions.q: What does the Product Owner actually own in Scrum?
options: The backlog's priority order — deciding what gets built next
Writing all the code for the sprint
Running the Daily Scrum as the team's manager
Fixing the team's broken test environment
questions.explain: The Product Owner is the single person accountable for the backlog's priority order, deciding what the team builds next based on business needs.

questions.q: What is the Scrum Master's job during a sprint?
options: Facilitating Scrum ceremonies and removing blockers for the team
Deciding which backlog items are most important
Writing the user stories themselves
Approving every pull request before it merges
questions.explain: The Scrum Master doesn't manage the work itself — they facilitate ceremonies like standup and the retrospective, and clear whatever is blocking the Developers.

questions.q: What is the Daily Scrum actually for?
options: The team synchronizing with itself on progress and blockers, not a status report to a manager
A formal performance review of each developer
Deciding the sprint's final budget
Demoing finished work to external stakeholders
questions.explain: The Daily Scrum (standup) is a short daily sync where the team coordinates with itself — it's not a status report delivered upward to a manager.

questions.q: Which of these is written in proper user story form?
options: As a sales manager, I want a dashboard filtered by region, so that I can spot underperforming territories without asking an analyst
Build a dashboard
The dashboard must load in under 2 seconds
Sprint 4 backlog item #12
questions.explain: A proper user story follows the "As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]" shape — describing the need from the user's point of view, not just a task label or a technical requirement.

questions.q: Why do acceptance criteria matter even when a user story already describes what the user wants?
options: Because a story on its own is often too vague to know when the work is actually finished — acceptance criteria give specific, checkable conditions
Because acceptance criteria replace the need for a Sprint Review
Because the Scrum Master is legally required to write them
They don't matter — a well-written story never needs them
questions.explain: A story describes the need, but acceptance criteria turn it into a shared, checkable definition of done — specific conditions the finished work must satisfy before it counts as complete.
